tts: The world's best-selling cognac was founded by an Irish soldier. And most of it is drunk in America.
Richard Hennessy served the King of France, settled in a small town called Cognac, and in seventeen sixty-five started his own trading house.
His descendants put stars on the labels, and in eighteen seventy they created X.O., for extra old.
Since eighteen-oh-six, one family, the Fillioux, has guarded the taste. Today it's the eighth generation.
In America, the brand was one of the first to advertise in magazines for Black readers, and in nineteen sixty-three it made a Black Olympic medalist a vice president.
Hip-hop carried that loyalty forward: Tupac and dozens of rappers sang about Henny. Today, the U.S. is the brand's biggest market.
In nineteen seventy-one, Hennessy merged with Moët champagne, and later with Louis Vuitton. That's the H in LVMH.
Today it's roughly forty percent of all cognac. But last year, tariffs in the U.S. and China hit even the king of cognac.
